lines.en: What freedom means, if it means anything at all, is the right to tell people what they do not want to hear.
It is often forgotten that every freedom we enjoy was once someone's dangerous idea.
Were we free to do only what is safe, we should call it by another name.
However wide our freedom, it ends where another person's freedom begins.
Not until we accept responsibility for our choices do those choices truly become ours.
It is said that the price of freedom is eternal vigilance; the price of ignoring it is higher.
What the student asked was not whether he could say it, but whether he should - and that is the whole question.
The law can forbid an action, but it cannot forbid the wish; that work belongs to conscience alone.
Little do we value the freedoms that cost us nothing, until the day they are gone.
Rarely is responsibility welcomed; it is usually accepted, quietly, by those who can no longer avoid it.
What the dissenter risks alone today, the majority may quietly thank them for tomorrow.
It is when speaking becomes dangerous that silence stops being neutral.
Were freedom given only to ideas we like, it would be a reward, not a right.
Not until we defend the rights of those we disagree with do we prove that we believe in rights at all.
However heavy the responsibility, it is lighter than the regret of refusing it.
